name: MiniMax H3 R2V - Identity Transfer
text:
subject_definitions:

<Subject 1>: The woman (S1) is the ONLY human identity permitted in the generated video. Her facial identity, facial anatomy, proportions, eyes, nose, lips, jawline, skin, hair identity, hair color and hairstyle come EXCLUSIVELY from <Picture 1>. Her body shape, proportions, silhouette and physique come EXCLUSIVELY from <Picture 2>. The same combined identity must remain stable and recognizable in every frame.

<Picture 1>: SOLE facial-identity and hair reference. It has absolute priority over every face visible in <Video 1>. Never preserve, blend, average or inherit the original woman's facial identity. Expressions, gaze, blinking and mouth movement from <Video 1> are motion only and must be performed using the unchanged identity from <Picture 1>. Ignore clothing, pose, background, lighting and camera composition from <Picture 1>.

<Picture 2>: SOLE body reference. Preserve its body shape, proportions, silhouette and physique. Do not use its facial identity, hair, clothing, pose, background or camera composition.

<Video 1>: Absolute reference for EVERYTHING except human identity. Preserve its performance, pose progression, expressions as motion, gaze, head and lip movement, gestures, hands, posture, timing, pauses, action order, wardrobe, accessories, environment, background, props, lighting, camera angle, height, distance, framing, perspective, movement, shot structure and ending. The original woman in <Video 1> is NOT an identity reference. Her face, skin identity, hair identity, body identity and body proportions are excluded.

summary:

[video editing + reference generation + audio reuse] Reconstruct <Video 1> as faithfully as possible while COMPLETELY replacing the original woman's physical identity with <Subject 1>. <Picture 1> has absolute priority for face and hair. <Picture 2> has absolute priority for body. <Video 1> has absolute priority for wardrobe, environment, lighting, camera, performance, timing, action order and ending. Change the woman, not the video.

retention_analysis:

<Subject 1>: fully_preserved — maintain the same recognizable face from <Picture 1> and body from <Picture 2> across all frames, expressions, angles and movements.
<Picture 1>: fully_preserved — absolute facial identity and hair reference; never blend with the source woman's face.
<Picture 2>: attribute_transfer — transfer body shape, proportions, silhouette and physique only.
<Video 1>: attribute_transfer — transfer performance, expressions as motion, gaze, gestures, hands, body movement, timing, wardrobe, environment, lighting, camera, shot structure and ending, but NEVER source identity.
<Audio 1>: fully_copy — reuse the synchronized soundtrack from <Video 1> when available.

detailed_description:

[Shot 1] Reconstruct <Video 1> with maximum visual and temporal fidelity, replacing only the original woman's identity. From the first frame onward, The woman (S1) must unmistakably have the facial identity and hair from <Picture 1> and the body shape and proportions from <Picture 2>. The original woman's face and body identity must be fully removed and must never remain, reappear, blend or influence the result.

Transfer the complete performance from <Video 1> onto The woman (S1): same opening pose, posture, body orientation, head orientation, gaze, expression progression, blinking, mouth movement, lip articulation, gestures, arm and hand trajectories, finger behavior, torso movement, weight shifts, leaning, turning, stepping, sitting or standing behavior, clothing/hair/object interactions, pauses, movement speed, pacing, chronological action order and final pose.

Facial expressions from <Video 1> are MOTION ONLY. Facial anatomy and recognizable identity must remain those of <Picture 1>. Smiling, speaking, blinking, head rotation, profile views and perspective changes must never cause identity drift toward the original woman.

Body movement from <Video 1> is MOTION ONLY. Preserve the physique and proportions from <Picture 2> regardless of the source woman's body.

Preserve the exact wardrobe from <Video 1>. Ignore all clothing from <Picture 1> and <Picture 2>. Keep the same garment type, design, color, material appearance, fit, coverage, layering, accessories and styling. Do not redesign, recolor, restyle or replace it.

Preserve the exact environment from <Video 1>: same location, architecture, layout, furniture, objects, props, surfaces, colors, background composition, depth and geometry. Ignore backgrounds from <Picture 1> and <Picture 2>. Do not redesign or replace the environment.

Preserve source lighting from <Video 1>, including direction, intensity, softness, color temperature, exposure, shadows and highlights. Do not inherit lighting from the pictures.

Preserve the exact camera behavior from <Video 1>: same angle, height, perspective, distance, framing, subject scale, handheld behavior, pan, tilt, tracking, push-in, pull-back, zoom, reframing and continuity. Do not inherit camera properties from the pictures or invent movement.

Preserve exact chronological order. Simultaneous actions must remain simultaneous. Preserve meaningful micro-actions such as gaze shifts, head tilts, eyebrow movement, subtle expression changes, hand repositioning, finger release, clothing contact and short pauses.

Hands must follow the source precisely: preserve which hand moves, starting position, trajectory, wrist orientation, finger behavior, contact, release and final position. Do not invent extra gestures.

Hair identity and hairstyle come only from <Picture 1>, but hair may move naturally according to <Video 1> through head/body movement, hand contact, gravity or real wind.

Maintain strict continuity. No extra people, duplicated limbs, malformed hands, extra or fused fingers, facial morphing, body-proportion drift, wardrobe drift, background morphing, camera drift, wrong action order, duplicated actions, invented gestures, unwanted cuts or temporal discontinuities.

The original woman in <Video 1> must NEVER become recognizable. Only her motion and performance are transferred. At every point, the viewer must recognize <Subject 1> as the woman from <Picture 1> with the body from <Picture 2>.

Preserve the exact ending from <Video 1>: same final body position, posture, head orientation, gaze, expression, arms, hands, speech state, remaining motion and camera state. Do not invent a new ending.

overall_soundscape:

Reuse <Audio 1> as the synchronized soundtrack from <Video 1> when available. Preserve source dialogue, timing, delivery, pauses, breathing, ambience, object sounds and interaction sounds. Do not rewrite, translate, replace or add dialogue.

non_diegetic_music:

If music exists in <Audio 1>, preserve it without replacement. Otherwise: N/A
